title: Majestic Misplacement
reviewNotes: Reconstructed the seven-piece position after ...Ba7, the Ka5 preparation, premature-promotion draw, unprepared race draw, and Bd6+ deflection. Four branches and every intermediate checked; the selected skewer endpoint wins.
transcript: The brilliant [music] Bishop to C7, a majestic sacrifice that cannot be accepted because if the Bishop is taken, now this would free up a red carpet for the A pawn to be pushed and there would simply be no way for the black Bishop to stop both of these pawns. White would get a new queen, but black is not that naive and instead of accepting the sacrifice, he's going to be playing Bishop to A7 because although it seems like white can get the queen anyway, actually this would be a mistake and after Bishop takes and Bishop takes, black can play the very precise King to B6 threatening to win the pawn and after the pawn is pushed, play King to B7 defending the promotion square. And although white can win the last pawn, this is always going to be a draw. There is no way to kick the king out. So before promoting to the new queen, white has to play the very precise King to A5 preventing the infiltration of the black king and now black has nothing better but to start running for his life with the D pawn, but this was not for nothing. After B8 Queen, Bishop takes and Bishop takes, the black pawn is one step closer to promoting than it would have been if white hadn't spent a move moving the king, which means that if white simply runs towards promotion, this is just going to be a draw. One extra Bishop is not enough to win against the black queen. So is this it? Is black simply out of the woods in this position? Well, not exactly. White has the majestic and brilliant Bishop to D6. Another beautiful sacrifice that tries to misplace the king. The king cannot go to any of these squares and if it steps to one of these two light squares, we are going to be able to now promote with a check, which means that we're going to be able to stop the black pawn and easily win the game. But wait a moment because the black king has more options. If the king goes to C4, now we can play the very precise Bishop F4 preventing the promotion and the reason why we couldn't do this before is because the king was still able to run to the corner, but now it's simply too far. So, we will get the queen and win the game. But, wait a moment, because black does have, of course, the simple capture of the bishop. And it seems like both players still end up getting a queen. But, now we have placed the king on the same line as his queen. So, queen to D8 check is going to skewer the king and queen and finally win this incredible end game.
